newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Essar phone network restored after fire.
newsitem.headline: India's Essar phone network restored after fire.

text.p: India's Essar group said a fire in an office building in New Delhi on Tuesday knocked out its cellular telephone services in the capital but they were restored after a brief interruption.

Essar has an office on the first floor of the Chandralok Building of New Delhi's Connaught Place area. A fire broke out on the ninth floor of the building at about 9 a.m. (0330 GMT) and was still burning three hours later.

An Essar official who asked not to be identified told Reuters that the fire had not reached the firm's offices but the cellular network automatically switched off due to the heat. Service was later restored.
"Everything is back to normal," he said.
Essar is the majority shareholder in Sterling Cellular Ltd, which has been granted licences to provide cellular telephone services in Delhi and three other zones.
Essar's partner is Swiss Telecom PTT, which was recently authorised to raise its stake in Sterling to 32.65 percent from 30.
